identity_check: Confirmed as Magentic (magentic.com), the London startup with a New York office that builds AI agents ('Mages', 'digital workers') for procurement and supply-chain work at global manufacturers. The company site (home, about, customers, its Series A story), Sequoia's 'Partnering with Magentic' post, Pulse 2.0 (July 2025) and TheNextWeb (September 2026) all describe the same company and the same co-founders, Robin Van Aeken (CEO, ex-McKinsey) and Odhran O'Donoghue (CTO, ex-OpenAI, Oxford PhD); Sequoia's investor file links the same domain. Not the open-source Python LLM library also called 'magentic', and not Microsoft's 'Magentic-One' agent system. Category set to direct (not in the PROJECT_CONTEXT §7 seed list; candidate from Sequoia's portfolio): Magentic's agents do procurement work for manufacturers — supplier selection, contract negotiation, ordering, invoice processing, price-leakage and MRO-spend recovery — across direct and indirect spend, which is Utopian Autonomy's procurement wedge. Differences: it sells to procurement and supply-chain teams at large global manufacturers (Siemens is the one named customer; beverage, consumer-goods and pharma clients are anonymised), its agents talk over Microsoft Teams and email inside the customer's ERP, and no page mentions WhatsApp, plant-floor staff, maintenance, process stability or engineering drawings. Layer plant_ops is the nearest fit (no supply-chain layer in the taxonomy), as for Didero.

company.name: Magentic
company.description: London startup (New York office) building AI agents that carry out procurement and supply-chain work inside global manufacturers' ERPs, talking to staff over Teams and email.

layer_detail: Procurement / supply-chain back office rather than the plant floor: multi-agent 'Mages' that read contracts, ERP records, invoices, emails and spreadsheets to find savings before a purchase, protect value during it (supplier selection, negotiation, ordering) and recover value after it (price leakage, invoice errors, MRO spend). Direct and indirect spend; humans approve major decisions. Users are procurement and supply-chain teams reached over Microsoft Teams and email. 'plant_ops' is the nearest layer; there is no supply-chain layer in the taxonomy.
product_summary: Multi-agent 'digital workers' that plug into a manufacturer's ERP, contracts, invoices and inboxes to run procurement tasks end to end: hunting savings, choosing suppliers, negotiating, placing orders, processing invoices and recovering price leakage, coordinating with staff over Teams and email while people sign off key decisions.
